record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Must every aperiodic infinite word have factors of arbitrarily large palindromic length?

evidence.quote: (due to Frid, Puzynina and Zamboni, [29, p. 738]): Every aperiodic infinite word has factors of arbitrarily high palindromic length. Then, he proved that this conjecture is in fact equivalent to the following one:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. Let A be a finite alphabet. A finite word over A is a palindrome if it reads the same from left to right as from right to left. The palindromic length PL(w) of a nonempty finite word w is the least integer k ≥ 1 such that w can be written as a concatenation w = p_1 p_2 ··· p_k of nonempty palindromes p_1, …, p_k over A. A factor of an infinite word u = u_0 u_1 u_2 ··· (u_i ∈ A) is any finite word of the form u_i u_{i+1} ··· u_{j-1} with 0 ≤ i ≤ j. An infinite word u is called periodic if there exists T ≥ 1 such that u_{n+T} = u_n for all n ≥ 0, and is called aperiodic otherwise.

Question. Prove or disprove: for every aperiodic infinite word u over a finite alphabet A and every integer N ≥ 1, there exists a factor w of u with PL(w) ≥ N. Equivalently, must the set {PL(w) : w is a factor of u} be unbounded for every aperiodic infinite word u?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (originating with Frid, Puzynina and Zamboni, 2013) remains open in full generality. It has been proven in several substantial cases: for all k-power-free words, for Sturmian words, and for a class covering "almost all" aperiodic infinite words; further partial results concern prefix palindromic length of automatic words such as the Thue–Morse and Sierpinski words. No complete proof or counterexample for arbitrary aperiodic infinite words is known.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic Length in Free Monoids and Free Groups
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture was first formulated by Frid, Puzynina and Zamboni; partial results show it holds for k-power-free words and for almost all aperiodic words.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture stated and proved in special cases; remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Prefix palindromic length of the Thue-Morse word (arXiv:1906.09392)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies prefix palindromic length for the Thue–Morse word, contributing partial evidence toward the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Active partial progress on related prefix-palindromic version.

status_evidence.title: Palindromic Length of Words with Many Periodic Palindromes (arXiv:2005.01371)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates palindromic length under structural assumptions giving further partial cases of the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress; conjecture still not settled in general.
